title: Chapter Map
notes: Open with the scope of the chapter rather than a technical definition. The first arc treats complex structures on a fixed differentiable manifold as points in an infinite-dimensional space, then studies the integrability equations infinitesimally. The second arc changes viewpoint: a deformation is a family over a base, and local moduli are described by Kodaira-Spencer and Kuranishi theory.

title: Rigid Vs Moduli
notes: Use the torus as the motivating mental picture. Varying a lattice in the complex plane changes the complex structure on the same underlying differentiable torus, while changing tau by a modular transformation may produce an isomorphic complex torus. This is the reason the chapter must discuss both equations for complex structures and quotients by equivalence.

title: Quotient By Diffeomorphisms
notes: The quotient slide is the conceptual setup for printed pages 255 to 256. The set of all almost complex structures is larger and better behaved than the integrable locus. Integrability cuts out a nonlinear subset, and even after solving that equation one must divide by the diffeomorphism group because different tensors can define isomorphic complex manifolds.

title: Graph Deformation
notes: This slide translates a moving complex structure into a form-valued tangent vector. For a small deformation, the new antiholomorphic tangent bundle can be written as the graph of a bundle map from the old T zero one into T one zero. The compactness assumption in the source keeps the smallness condition harmless.

title: Bracket Closure
notes: Keep the geometric meaning visible before writing the Maurer-Cartan formula. Integrability means the antiholomorphic directions close under the Lie bracket. If the bracket of two graph sections has a component transverse to the graph, that component is the residual that obstructs integrability.

title: Maurer-Cartan Residual
notes: Now give the formula. The bracket in A zero star of T X combines the Lie bracket of vector fields with wedge product in the form direction. The Maurer-Cartan residual is a nonlinear map from graph parameters to A zero two of T X, and the integrable deformations are its zero set.

title: Power-Series Recursion
notes: This is the computational heart of the first section. The first equation says phi one is dbar closed. At every later order, the lower coefficients have already produced a bracket source. The next coefficient exists only if this source can be killed by applying dbar to something.

title: Kodaira-Spencer Class
notes: Connect the algebra to the quotient by diffeomorphisms. The first coefficient of the deformation is dbar closed, so it defines a Dolbeault cohomology class. A first-order deformation coming only from a one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms gives an exact class. Therefore H one of the tangent sheaf is the true first-order deformation space.

title: Obstruction In H2
notes: Emphasize that obstruction is not philosophical here; it is visible in the second recursive equation. The bracket of the first-order representative gives a closed A zero two of T X form. If its cohomology class in H two of T X is nonzero, no choice of phi two can solve the equation.

title: Calabi-Yau Contraction
notes: The Calabi-Yau hypothesis enters through a concrete isomorphism, not through a metric at first. A nowhere vanishing holomorphic volume form converts polyvector fields into forms by contraction. This is the bridge that lets the Tian-Todorov argument translate bracket expressions into exact form statements.

title: Delta Is Not The Laplacian
notes: Pause on the warning because the symbol Delta can mislead students. Here Delta is eta inverse composed with partial composed with eta, so it is a differential on polyvector-valued forms. It squares to zero and anti-commutes with dbar, but it is unrelated to the Laplacian until a metric is introduced later for Hodge choices.

title: Tian-Todorov Proof Move
notes: State the proof move rather than the full coordinate proof. Tian-Todorov identifies the bracket with the failure of Delta to satisfy a Leibniz rule. When the inputs are Delta closed, this makes the bracket Delta exact. Combined with the Calabi-Yau contraction and the dbar partial lemma, this is what kills the obstruction terms.

title: Formal CY Solution Ledger
notes: Present the proposition as a ledger of obligations. Each order produces a residual from previous choices. In the Calabi-Yau Kahler setting, the Tian-Todorov lemma and Hodge theoretic exactness make that residual solvable, so the formal Maurer-Cartan equation can be solved to all orders. Mention that convergence is a separate analytic issue, with stronger metric input used in the source remarks.

title: Families Of Complex Manifolds
notes: Shift from equations to families, following printed pages 268 to 270. The examples are meant to prevent a naive view of families: locally trivial, globally nontrivial, effectively parametrizing, and special-fiber behavior are different phenomena. Ehresmann says proper differentiable families are locally products, while Fischer-Grauert says a proper complex family with all fibres isomorphic is locally trivial holomorphically.

title: KS Map And Complex Spaces
notes: Use the exact sequence to connect the family viewpoint back to H one of T X. A tangent vector on the base lifts locally to vector fields on the total space, and the obstruction to gluing those lifts is the Kodaira-Spencer class. Complex spaces enter because the double point is the clean base for first-order deformations.

title: Complete Versal Kuranishi
notes: End by naming the local moduli theorem and the vocabulary students will see in applications. Complete means the family captures all nearby deformations by pullback, universal adds uniqueness, and versal keeps only first-order uniqueness. Kuranishi guarantees a versal family for any compact complex manifold, while unobstructedness means the base is smooth; H two vanishing and the Calabi-Yau Tian-Todorov result are the main criteria in this chapter.
